key_points: Hash‑map solution: iterate once, for each number x check if target‑x exists in the map; if not, store x.

key_points: Compute a sorted character string or frequency signature for each word and use it as a hash key to group anagrams.

Space O(N·K) for the groups.

key_points: First pass compute left products, second pass multiply by right products in output array.
Store result directly in output array to achieve O(1) extra space.
O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space (output array excluded).

key_points: Kadane’s algorithm: keep running sum and best sum while scanning the array.
Time O(n), space O(1).
Works with all‑negative arrays by initializing best to the first element.

key_points: In‑place rotation by 90° clockwise: first transpose the matrix, then reverse each row.

Alternative layer‑by‑layer four‑swap method also O(n^2) time, O(1) space.

key_points: Break the number into billions, millions, thousands and remainder; convert each chunk (0‑999) using a helper that handles hundreds, tens, and units.

key_points: Maintain running prefix sum and hashmap from sum to earliest index.
If currentSum‑k exists in map, subarray [map[sum‑k]+1, i] sums to k.
O(n) time, O(n) space for hashmap.
Works with negative numbers, k = 0, and multiple possible subarrays.

key_points: Use a frequency map (hash table) to count occurrences of each number.
Identify the element with the highest frequency; the optimal subarray is the segment of that element.

records.text: Max Difference You Can Get From Changing an Integer
key_points: Treat the integer as a string of digits; try changing each digit to any other digit (0‑9).
For each position compute the new value and track the maximum absolute difference from the original.
Time: O(d) where d = number of digits (≤10 for 32‑bit int); Space: O(1).
Edge cases: leading zero after change (ignore if it creates a shorter number), single‑digit numbers.

key_points: Build a map from website to list of timestamps per user (hash table of hash tables).
For each user, slide a window of size 3 over the sorted timestamps to generate 3‑website sequences.
Count each sequence across all users with another hash map; return the most frequent (lexicographically smallest on tie).

records.text: Find First and Last Position of Element in Sorted Array
key_points: Apply two binary searches on the sorted array: one to find the leftmost occurrence, another for the rightmost.

key_points: For each point, compute slopes to all other points using a hash map (dy/dx reduced to simplest form).
The maximum count for a given base point plus one gives the line size; track global maximum.
Time: O(n^2) for n points; Space: O(n) per iteration for the slope map.
Handle vertical lines (infinite slope) and duplicate points separately.

key_points: Classic sliding window with a hash set (or frequency map) to maintain unique characters.
Expand right pointer until a duplicate appears, then shrink left pointer to remove the duplicate.

key_points: Two‑pointer technique: start with left at 0, right at end; compute area = (right‑left) * min(height[left], height[right]).

key_points: Apply DFS or BFS to explore each connected component of '1's, marking visited cells to avoid recounting.
Iterate the grid; when a '1' is found, increment island count and launch a flood fill to mark the whole island.
Time complexity O(m·n) for an m×n grid; space complexity O(m·n) in worst case for recursion stack or explicit queue.

key_points: Represent courses as a directed graph and detect if a topological ordering exists.
Apply DFS with three‑state visitation (unvisited, visiting, visited) to detect cycles.
If any back edge is found, a cycle exists → return false; otherwise true.
Time O(V + E), space O(V + E) for adjacency list and recursion stack/visited array.

key_points: Breadth‑first search (multi‑source) from all initially rotten oranges; each level represents one minute.
Use a queue to process cells; for each rotten orange, infect adjacent fresh oranges and enqueue them.
Time: O(m·n) for grid size; Space: O(m·n) worst‑case for queue.

key_points: Bidirectional BFS between beginWord and endWord to reduce search space.
At each level, generate all one‑letter transformations; only keep those present in the word list.
Time: O(N·L·26) where N = number of words, L = word length; Space: O(N) for visited sets.
Edge cases: beginWord not in list, no possible transformation, start equals end.

key_points: First label each existing island with a unique id using DFS/BFS and store its area in a map.
Then for each water cell (0), compute potential island size by summing areas of distinct neighboring island ids plus 1 for the flipped cell.
Track the maximum size found; if the grid contains only land, answer is N·M (or N·M‑1 if a flip is required).
Time complexity O(N·M) for labeling and a second pass; space O(N·M) for the id matrix and area map.

records.text: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
key_points: Recursive DFS: return true if current node is p or q; propagate up if both sides return true.
When a node has one true from left and one from right, or itself is p/q and one side true, that node is LCA.
Time O(N) – visit each node once; Space O(H) recursion stack, H = height of tree.
Edge cases: one node is ancestor of the other; tree may be skewed (stack depth).

records.text: Binary Tree Zigzag Level Order Traversal
key_points: Use BFS with a queue; toggle a boolean flag each level to decide left‑to‑right or right‑to‑left order.
When the flag is false, reverse the list of node values for that level before adding to result (or prepend children in opposite order).
Time complexity O(N) – each node visited once; Space O(W) where W is the maximum width of the tree (queue size).
Edge cases: empty tree, single node tree, and handling null children while building each level.

key_points: Post‑order DFS returning height of subtree; at each node compute leftHeight and rightHeight, update global max with leftHeight + rightHeight.
Diameter is number of edges on longest path, so return maxDiameter.
Time O(N); Space O(H) recursion stack.
Edge cases: tree with single node (diameter 0); completely unbalanced tree (height = N‑1).

key_points: Choose a deterministic representation – e.g., preorder traversal with sentinel (e.g., "#") for null nodes.
Serialize: DFS preorder, appending node values and sentinel separated by commas; Deserialize: read tokens recursively rebuilding the tree.
Both operations run in O(N) time and O(N) space for the output string / recursion stack.

key_points: Build a Trie of all words; then for each board cell run DFS backtracking following Trie edges, collecting words when a terminal node is reached.
Mark visited cells during a path and restore after backtrack; prune branches when no further Trie child exists.
Time complexity roughly O(M·4^L) worst‑case (M = board cells, L = max word length) but heavily pruned by the Trie; Space O(T) for Trie plus O(L) recursion stack.
Edge cases: duplicate words in the list (store a flag to avoid repeats), words that are prefixes of others, and boards with a single row/column.

key_points: Model the alien alphabet as a directed graph where an edge u→v means u comes before v, derived from the first differing character of consecutive words.
Perform topological sort (Kahn's BFS or DFS) to produce a valid ordering; detect cycles to return empty or error.
Time O(C+U) where C is total characters in all words and U is number of unique letters; Space O(U+E) for graph structures.
Edge cases: prefix situation (e.g., "abc" before "ab" → invalid), isolated letters with no edges, and multiple valid orders (any topological order is acceptable).

key_points: Backtracking DFS from each cell, marking visited cells, and matching characters sequentially against the target word.
Prune early when the current board character does not match the word character; restore visited marks on backtrack.
Time O(M·4^L) worst case (M cells, L word length), Space O(L) recursion stack plus O(1) extra board marking.
Edge cases: word longer than total cells, repeated letters causing revisits, single‑cell board, and early termination when word is found.

key_points: Treat each equation a / b = k as a weighted edge a→b with weight k; the graph is a set of connected components.
Answer queries by finding a path between numerator and denominator and multiplying edge weights; use Union‑Find with weight ratios or DFS/BFS per query.
Union‑Find with path compression stores relative ratios, giving near O(α(N)) per union/find; total O(N + Q·α(N)). DFS approach is O(N+Q·E).
Edge cases: variables that never appear, division by zero not present by problem guarantee, and disconnected components returning -1.0.

records.text: Kth Largest Element in an Array
key_points: Use a min‑heap of size k to keep the k largest elements seen so far.
Iterate through the array: push element, and if heap size exceeds k, pop the smallest.
After processing, the heap root is the k‑th largest element.
Time O(n log k), space O(k). Alternative quick‑select gives average O(n) time, O(1) extra space.
Edge cases: k = 1 (max element), k = array length (min element), and handling duplicates.

key_points: Count frequencies with a hash map, then extract the k most frequent using a min‑heap of size k.
Push each (frequency, element) onto the heap; if heap size exceeds k, pop the smallest frequency.

key_points: Use a min‑heap (priority queue) containing the head of each list; repeatedly extract the smallest node and push its next node.

key_points: Maintain two heaps: a max‑heap for the lower half and a min‑heap for the upper half; keep sizes balanced (size diff ≤ 1).
Insert: push into appropriate heap then rebalance; Median is top of max‑heap (odd count) or average of tops (even count).

key_points: Greedy using a max‑heap of character frequencies; repeatedly pop two most frequent distinct chars and append them, decrement counts, and push back if still >0.
If one character remains with count > (n+1)/2, impossible – return empty string.
Time O(N log Σ) where Σ is alphabet size (constant 26 for lowercase), effectively O(N); Space O(Σ) for counts plus O(N) for result.

key_points: Count frequencies of tasks; the schedule length is max( (maxFreq‑1)*(cooldown+1) + countMaxFreq, totalTasks ).
Explanation: arrange the most frequent task with idle slots; fill slots with other tasks; if enough tasks, no idle time.
Time O(N) to count and compute; Space O(Σ) for frequency map (Σ = number of distinct tasks).
Edge cases: cooldown = 0 (answer = N), all tasks identical, and when number of tasks fills all idle slots eliminating idle time.

records.text: Maximize Y-Sum by Picking a Triplet of Distinct X-Values
key_points: Group points by their x‑value; for each distinct x keep the top three y‑values (or use a max‑heap of size 3).

Iterate over all pairs of distinct x‑values (O(M²) where M = number of distinct x); for each pair take the best y from each side and compute candidate sum = y1 + y2 + maxYOverall where the third x is different from the first two.
Overall O(M²) time, O(M) space for storing top‑3 per x; works because M ≤ N and typical constraints keep M moderate.
Edge cases: fewer than three distinct x‑values (return 0 or appropriate sentinel), duplicate y values, and handling negative coordinates.

key_points: Greedy using a min‑heap of stick lengths; repeatedly pop two smallest sticks, add their sum to total cost, and push the sum back.
This is analogous to Huffman coding – always merging the two smallest yields minimal total cost.
Time O(N log N) for N sticks (heap operations); Space O(N) for the heap.
Edge cases: single stick (cost 0), already sorted input (heap still needed), and large integer sums requiring 64‑bit type.

key_points: Use a sweep line with a max‑heap (priority queue) to process building start and end edges sorted by x‑coordinate.
When encountering a start edge, push its height; when encountering an end edge, remove that height (lazy deletion).
After each event, the current max height from the heap determines the skyline height; record a key point when it changes.

records.text: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
key_points: Traverse the array from right to left and maintain a balanced BST (e.g., SortedList) or Fenwick tree to count smaller elements already seen.
For each element, query the tree for the count of values < current value, then insert the current value.
Fenwick tree with coordinate compression gives O(N log N) time and O(N) space; BST gives O(N log N) average.

key_points: Maintain a min‑heap of size k containing the k largest elements seen so far.
When a new number arrives, push it onto the heap; if heap size exceeds k, pop the smallest element.
The top of the min‑heap is always the k‑th largest element in the stream.
Each insertion is O(log k) time, O(k) space; retrieving the k‑th largest is O(1).

key_points: Expand Around Center: for each index treat it as a center of odd and even length palindrome and expand while characters match.
Track longest palindrome start and length during expansion.
Time complexity: O(n²) worst case; Space complexity: O(1).
Manacher's algorithm can achieve O(n) time with O(n) extra space if optimal solution is required.
Edge cases: all identical characters, empty string, single character string.

key_points: Dynamic programming: dp[i] = minimum coins needed to make amount i; initialize dp[0]=0 and others to INF.
Iterate amounts from 1..target and for each coin update dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i‑coin]+1).
Time complexity O(N·M) where N is number of coin types and M is the amount; space O(M).
If dp[amount] stays INF, return -1 (no solution).

key_points: Track both maximum and minimum product ending at each position because a negative number can flip signs.
Iterate once, updating curMax = max(num, curMax·num, curMin·num) and curMin = min(num, curMaxPrev·num, curMinPrev·num).
Maintain globalMax as the maximum curMax seen.
Time O(N) and space O(1).
Edge cases: zeros reset both products, all negative numbers, single‑element array.

key_points: Greedy linear scan keeping the farthest reachable index (maxReach).
For each index i ≤ maxReach, update maxReach = max(maxReach, i + nums[i]); if maxReach reaches or exceeds last index, return true.
If i exceeds maxReach before the end, return false.
Time O(N), space O(1).
Edge cases: first element 0 with length >1 (immediate false), large jumps, single‑element array.

records.text: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
key_points: Track the minimum price seen so far and the maximum profit achievable at each step.
Update minPrice = min(minPrice, price[i]) and maxProfit = max(maxProfit, price[i] - minPrice).
Time complexity: O(n) single pass; Space complexity: O(1).
Works for both increasing, decreasing, and fluctuating price sequences.
Edge cases: empty or single‑day array (profit 0), all prices decreasing (profit 0).

key_points: Use DFS with memoization to build all sentences; for each start index, try every word in the dictionary that matches the prefix.
Memo map from index to list of sentences formed from that suffix avoids recomputation.
Overall time is exponential in worst case but bounded by number of valid sentences; space O(N·L) for memo where L is average sentence length.
Handle edge cases: empty string, no possible segmentation (return empty list), duplicate words in dictionary.

key_points: Dynamic programming on intervals: dp[l][r] = max coins obtainable by bursting balloons in (l, r) exclusive.
Treat virtual balloons with value 1 at both ends; for each possible last burst k in (l, r), dp[l][r] = max(dp[l][k] + dp[k][r] + nums[l]*nums[k]*nums[r]).
Fill dp by increasing interval length; time O(N³), space O(N²).

Optimization: use bottom‑up loops; no better than O(N³) known for this problem.

key_points: DP where dp[i] = number of ways to decode the prefix of length i.
Transition: if s[i‑1] != '0' add dp[i‑1]; if two‑digit number formed by s[i‑2:i] is between 10 and 26, add dp[i‑2].
Initialize dp[0] = 1, dp[1] based on first character.

key_points: Dynamic programming: dp[i] = true if s[0:i] can be segmented; dp[0] = true.
For each position i, check all j < i where dp[j] is true and s[j:i] is in the word dictionary (hash set).

records.text: Server Allocation Cost, customers pick servers with most idle instances; cost = max + min idle before selection. Pattern: Heap simulation.
key_points: Maintain a max‑heap for idle instances per server and a min‑heap for the same values to retrieve max and min quickly.
When a customer picks a server, pop the max and min values, compute cost = max + min, then decrement the chosen server's idle count and push the updated value back into both heaps.
Each selection is O(log S) where S is the number of servers; overall space is O(S) for the two heaps.
Edge cases: only one server (max = min), servers running out of idle instances (remove from heap when count reaches zero).

For a candidate X, greedily assign items to warehouses keeping each warehouse’s stock ≤ X; count how many warehouses can be filled with ≤ X stock.

records.text: Minimum Array Operations, min ops so every subarray of length > 1 has non-negative sum. Pattern: Prefix-sum state reset.

Edge cases: already non‑negative array (zero ops), all negative numbers (one op per element).

Run the full test suite after each change; keep changes minimal to avoid side effects.
Complexity is irrelevant for debugging; focus on code readability and proper error handling.

records.text: Maximize bitwise AND of k elements after spending an increment budget. Pattern: Greedy bit by bit from the top with shared-budget accounting (OA, Sep 2026).
key_points: Greedy bit‑by‑bit from the most significant bit: try to set each bit in the answer, compute the minimum total increments needed to make at least k numbers have that bit set.
For a candidate bit, count how many numbers already have it; for the rest compute the cost to raise them to the next multiple that sets the bit (using (1<<b) - (x % (1<<b))).
If total cost ≤ budget, keep the bit and deduct the cost; otherwise skip it.
Time O(32·n) ≈ O(n), space O(1).
Edge cases: budget zero, k = 1 (just maximize a single element), all numbers already share high bits, overflow when adding increments.

records.text: Minimum priority conflicts when interleaving two lowercase strings. Pattern: Interleave preserving each string's order; a conflict is a lower-priority letter before a higher one; DP over (i, j) (OA, Sep 2026).
key_points: DP over positions (i, j) where i characters taken from first string and j from second; dp[i][j] = minimum conflicts so far.
When adding next character, add 1 if it is lower‑priority than any previously placed higher‑priority character (track highest priority seen).
Transition: dp[i+1][j] = min(dp[i+1][j], dp[i][j] + conflictCost(first[i])); similarly for second string.
Time O(|A|·|B|), space O(min(|A|,|B|)) by rolling array.
Edge cases: one string empty, all characters same priority, alternating priorities causing maximal conflicts.

records.text: Minimize grid inconvenience by adding one delivery center. Pattern: Multi-source BFS for Chebyshev distance, then binary search on the answer with a bounding-box feasibility check (OA, Sep 2026).
key_points: Run a multi‑source BFS from all existing delivery centers to compute Chebyshev distance (max of row/col diff) to every cell.
Binary search the minimal possible maximum distance D; for each D, check if there exists a cell whose distance to all existing centers ≤ D (i.e., intersection of D‑radius squares).
The feasibility check reduces to intersecting axis‑aligned squares; compute the overlapping rectangle and verify it is non‑empty.
Overall time O(N·M + log (maxDim)) where N·M is grid size for BFS; space O(N·M) for distance map.
Edge cases: grid of size 1×1, existing centers covering whole grid, D = 0 (must place on a cell already a center).

key_points: Maintain a min‑heap of size k containing the next element from each sorted stream; heap key is the event timestamp.
